summary: A 100-ft steel lookout with a 12x12 cab, said to have moved from Mississippi to Holston High Knob in 1943; its cab was torn off by 2004 and it is unstaffed.

facts.design: 100-ft steel tower with a 12x12-ft cab and catwalk
facts.status_note: A June 2004 visit report found the cab walls and roof torn off; the steel tower is listed as standing.

access.note: On Cherokee National Forest land. The register says the tower is now used on an emergency basis, and a hiking guide says it cannot be climbed.

visit.trail_note: A hiking guide notes good views from the summit, but says the tower itself cannot be climbed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's 4,117 ft (1,255 m) matches the record and is kept. Wikipedia and the hiking guide give 4,136 ft and TN Landforms gives 4137 ft; the gap is small and no source explains it.

The register's June 2004 visit report says the cab was torn off, and TN Landforms lists the tower as standing. Wikipedia describes an old dismantled fire tower with a communications tower on the site. The record keeps 'standing' with a status note; no source after 2004 was found.

notes_for_editor: The Mississippi origin and the 1943 move rest on the NHLR register. The Komoot guide repeats both and may have taken them from the register, so they are not independent confirmations. No source dates the wooden predecessor; 1934 is inferred from 'nine years earlier'. Current status is unclear: the last visit report is June 2004 (cab torn off), TN Landforms says standing, and Wikipedia says dismantled with a communications tower. Access level 'restricted' is our reading of the register's emergency-only use and the guide's 'cannot be climbed'; no official access notice was found. The 100-ft figure is the register's tower height and is not confirmed as height to the cab floor, so height_m is omitted.
